<summary>Text description of this diagram</summary>

Three boxes in a row, joined left to right, with an arrow looping from the third back to the
first so that the three read as a circuit. The first two happen in Phase 5 and the third in
Phase 1 of the next piece of work.

1. **Record the lesson**, where the next analyst will look for it. For a regular output that is
   the analytical plan for the next cycle.
2. **Raise it wider**, for anything that applies beyond this one output: a method that did not
   work, a data quality problem, an assurance step that was disproportionate in either direction.
   The routes are in [who to ask](/guidance/09-resources/r3-who-to-ask.qmd).
3. **Use it at scoping.** Look for relevant lessons from earlier work when you scope the next
   piece, and capture new ones as they happen rather than reconstructing them at the end.

Under the row it reads: capture lessons as they happen, not by reconstructing them at the end. A
panel below is headed "where it is written down", and reads: the review record sits with the
project record, which for most outputs is a short entry in the analytical plan.

</details>
